ratings_why.fun: Gust is a real attack, so it overlaps with Cleave, Swoop, Pack, Bristle and Bitter for free, and the Thunderhead-versus-Crier seating and Föhn feeding the Windhover are the kind of tangles I draft for.
ratings_why.distinct: Announced makes play order a shop decision and lets any tribe's unit be the carry, which is fresh; the extra-attack core itself is closer to familiar 'attacks immediately' effects.

verdict_why: One real rules gap (does Lady High Pressure cancel enemy Gusts, including the ones Old Föhn forces?) needs a ruling; the rest can stay hot.

points.text: It's unclear whether enemy Gusts count as the 'first 3 attacks' Lady High Pressure cancels. The Föhn ruling calls his forced Gusts enemy attacks, so with both on board she would cancel Föhn's whole effect. Say which it is.
Old Föhn plus Lady High Pressure could be a deliberate combo instead of a clash: let her steal Föhn's forced Gusts, so each one becomes an Announced Gust.

The Barometer Clerk only checks a threshold. It would be more fun if it read the forecast, e.g. paying out by how many Gusts the last fight had, so it sits in the Gust count build instead of beside it.
Mr and Mrs Fair-and-Foul switching each turn could interact with Announced or reading order (Fair gives gold, Foul makes the Announced unit Gust), so the flip turns into a seating choice.
Red Sky at Night does one plain job. A reading-order or 'played last this turn' twist would let it join the seating puzzle the rest of the Court asks for.

standouts.why: 'First time it attacks or Gusts' turns the tribe's own Crier into a hazard, so you seat a non-Gale blocker in front of him on purpose.
Old Föhn makes the enemy Gust into Bristle, Bitter and the Windhover: a card used for things it doesn't mention.
Sir Vane copying your last play, changing tribe and possibly breaking the Crier's line ties the shop moment to fight order.

weakest.why: The Bag-Bearer is a plain delivery card; the Bag of Winds is the interesting part.
The Barometer Clerk is gold-or-stats with no decision once you pass 4 Gusts.
Mr and Mrs Fair-and-Foul flip on their own with nothing to play around.

flags.note: Whether enemy Gusts (Föhn's forced ones, an enemy Windhover's) count among the 3 cancelled attacks isn't written.
+20/+20 permanent per Announced unit a fight, doubled with the Helm and again golden; bounded per fight but grows fast.
Golden Sir Vane copying two Tier 6 cards, as the designer notes.
Cancelling all enemy Start of Combat effects nearly blanks an opposing Gale Court board, whose Gusts are mostly Start of Combat.
